question.text: A stock has intrinsic value Rs. 250 and market price Rs. 180. A PMS investor should:

answer.text: Buy — it appears undervalued, assuming transaction costs allow

explanation.text: The Logic: Source p.43 says an investor should buy when the market price is below intrinsic value and the difference is enough to cover transaction costs. With market price Rs. 180 below intrinsic value Rs. 250, the stock appears undervalued and is a buy candidate subject to the transaction-cost caveat. The Trap: Selling or shorting an apparently undervalued stock runs counter to the intrinsic-value rule on p.43. Note: Per p.43, the price gap must be large enough to cover transaction costs.
